passage:
A child brought a broken toy car to the repair table at the community fair. One wheel had fallen off, and the motor no longer worked.
The volunteer opened the car carefully. The child watched every step. They found a loose wire and fixed it. Then they replaced the wheel with one from an old toy box.
When the car moved again, the child shouted with joy.
The volunteer said, "Now you know a little about what is inside."
The child had come only to get a toy back. He left with curiosity.
Repairing something can save money and reduce waste, but it can also open a small door into how things work.
